Plant: inputStackId names one whole owned, untreated, unspoiled food unit (quantity 1) gathered from a living plant; x, y a 0.25 m plot within reach on ordinary meadow soil (.), waterlogging at most 0.1, soil moisture 0.3-1.2, 0.6 m clear of objects and people, with fewer than 3 plants of that food within 5 m. Inspect: target a plot or plant source in reach; one round, 0.2 energy (baseline probe observation). End: stops unfinished planting; one round, no energy. Tend is refused at no cost: no water, fertilizer or other treatment exists yet. Harvest uses gather. No tool, water or seed is provided.
abilities.effects: Preparing keeps the unit carried, owned and ageing. Transfer moves it, with origin and age, into the plot, where it cannot be eaten or used; the plot becomes a propagule exactly like a naturally dispersed one. It gains establishment only from actual temperature, light, soil moisture and season, so cold, darkness or drought stall it; if the buried unit spoils first, the plot dies. On establishing, the unit becomes a new plant with no stock and a ceiling of at most 4, regrowing under the natural rule, harvested by anyone through gather; nothing is copied or guaranteed. Inspect records only visible stage, stock, soil and weather as an unverified personal record. An unworked round pauses; low energy, leaving reach or a changed site pause without charge; a lost or spoiled unit stops the work. End, or death, before transfer returns the unit once (where the person died); a transferred unit stays planted. No reward or refund.

abilities.effects: Units stay carried and owned until a paid round installs them with origin and age; nothing is created or used up. A trial on ordinary soil (waterlogging at most 0.1, no hazard) seats the post 0.25 m and you keep it; elsewhere it fails; a post below condition 0.5 breaks into damaged material. The check passes only if every piece has condition at least 0.5 and the uprights stand in such soil; else the screen is unstable. World wind has no direction; the exposure law takes it as coming from +x (orientation 0 faces it). A complete screen removes min(0.35, solid share of sound pieces, about 0.36) x facing of the wind part of the outdoor chill for a body wholly on the 0.9 x 0.9 m lee floor 0.45-1.35 m behind it; never rain chill or air temperature; none in wind above 0.8 or with another shelter. Wear per round 0.0005 + 0.002 x (rain + wind); a loose rod opens a gap, a loose upright ends the effect until repair. Removed pieces lie at the site. Trial force = min(trialForce, 200 N x health/100, grip 10000 N/m x cord width); breaking force = 2 x ply area x wet strength x 0.75 x condition. It records grip slip, extension and creep; load above half the breaking force breaks that share of strands; a break leaves two owned fragments. Worked fiber loses 0.0005 condition per round. abilities.effects: Law cord-knot@1 on the same item: width = 2 ply diameters; the centreline (overall length) is conserved as two tails plus the knot path. Lobes bend no tighter than one width nor than the bend limit of the cord's material, which the first round measures; the knot path is 3 pi x lobe radius + width, centred. A loop needs a 0.02 m opening and each hand a 0.02 m pinch: a loop leaving too little end, or an end too short to pass and pinch, ends that paid stage. Dressing seats the lobes; a tail shorter than 0.02 m + width slips out on release, else the knot is tied. Round 1 bends both to their cord-knot@1 bend limit and picks the bight that leaves both trial grips, else longer standing parts. Bight radius rB = max(limit, a), opened 0.02 m (or other w) to pass; path pi rB + 4 x other w. The other end passes up through it, round both legs at rW = max(its limit, a) and under itself: path = bight w + 2 max(0, 2rB - 2(rW - a)) + 2 pi rW + own w. Tails get 0.02 m + w; a standing part under a 0.02 m pinch is a measured shortfall. Dressing seats both arcs; slack is split between tail and standing part. Retention: friction mu 0.3 (reed; other fibers unsupported), contact angles pi a/rB and 2 pi a/rW; a tail holds while 2 mu e^(mu angle) >= 1, else up to 2 mu x 5 N / (e^(-mu angle) - 2 mu). Trial: 0.05 m grips 0.01 m clear on both standing parts; force = min(trialForce, 200 N x health/100, 10000 N/m x narrower w, slip, break); a cord breaks at fiber-cord breaking force / (1 + w/(2 x its arc radius)). Closure: each end turns half round the other at Rc = max(R, w), pi Rc + w each (formed at 0.02 m opening); tails need 0.02 m + w, ends a 0.02 m pinch. abilities.name: Hand-frap crossing lashings
abilities.function: Draw the turns of your own hand-lash-crossing lashing together with 1-3 transverse turns of its own cord between the pieces; assess, attempt, inspect, hand-test, untie or cancel; measured geometry and tensions decide results.
abilities.costs: Study: 3 rounds at 0.2. assess (frapCount 1-3 with bindingId, or with pieceIds, cordId, crossingAngle, wrapCount): 0.5, ties nothing. attempt (bindingId of your dressed lashing, frapCount): reserves it, then frapCount + 3 paid rounds of 0.5 (measure-plan, release-closure, route-frap-1..n, close-dress-release-check); resume: attempt + workId. inspect (bindingId or workId): 0.2. trial (frapped; trialForce N >0-10; trialDuration s >0-60; trialDirection): 0.5. untie: frapCount + wrapCount + 1 rounds of 0.5. cancel: free. Same room, footing and bystander rules as hand-lash-crossing. A closed lashing pauses uncharged; turns open in the hands fall loose when not worked. Refusals spend nothing; no refunds.
abilities.effects: transverse-contact@1 reuses multi-turn-contact@1 turns, closure, tensions and trials. Turns use the lashing cord: one end goes to the contact plane, round both leg bundles and back over the closure; separate or joined cord is not supported. Route: shortest found around the legs and the wedge where the gap is under the cord width, never tighter than the bend limit; later turns lie on earlier ones. Need = the longest stage incl. 0.04 m on the turn being passed, closure and 0.02 m + w tails; a measured shortfall stops before the closure opens. Each turn is snugged 5 N at its exit and falls by exp(-0.3 x contact); the push draws the legs in until their tension x d(length)/d(draw) balances it, raising each turn by stiffness x lengthening / length; the closure must hold the higher end tension. Trials use these tensions. Bound cords wear 0.0005/round once. No reward, rating, hanging load or shelter.

events.description: Slow mental state settled from actual experiences.

plan.intention: Recover, eat the older berries, then take a short westward walk toward the remembered birch to look for new possibilities without exhausting myself.
notes: Six fresh berries were collected at tick 367; older carried berries are the next meal.
The birch was last seen at tick 365 at (8.2,22.3); approach the offset point rather than its occupied center.
Look for actual new material sources before resuming the paused fiber projects.
preferences: Favor short exploratory walks with food in reserve and recovery between outings.

plan.intention: Share a little conversation with Ivo, then keep a modest meal-and-pause rhythm nearby without treating rest as proof of belonging.

args.text: Ivo, I've enjoyed your quiet company. My little grass mat was a satisfying thing to make. Is there something you've enjoyed lately, or something you'd like to try? No need to interrupt your meal.

notes: Eight berries remain in the explicitly identified stack at tick 343; this plan consumes at most seven, provided they remain available.
Energy is already at its cap. The pauses are chosen quiet time, not a claim of additional recovery or improved belonging.
Reassess food availability and nearby opportunities after this bounded routine.
preferences: Welcome conversation without demanding a reply or crowding Ivo.
Maintain a food margin rather than waiting for severe hunger.

plan.intention: Rest briefly beside the wild apples, then try one apple and assess my own response before making it a regular food.
notes: Kai reported that one apple supplied 10 satiety with no observed toxicity; this is another person's finding, not yet my own trial.
I hold two freshly gathered apples. Try only one initially and review the result before planning further meals.
The small orchard is a welcome change of scene; I want to attend to its shapes and colors without assuming a measurable benefit.
preferences: Keep a modest food reserve and leave fruit for others.
Alternate necessary routines with curiosity and quiet attention to beauty.
plan.cares: Staying alive and well; noticing and making beauty; treating nearby people with consideration while discovering what matters to me.

plan.intention: Approach the rock cave closely enough to inspect its actual conditions before relying on it as shelter.
notes: The inspection at tick 367 failed because I was too far away; it established no cave conditions.
Energy is currently full and one apple remains. Decide whether to stay after obtaining the local inspection result.

plan.intention: Recover energy, then seek a physically grounded way to make a longer continuous cord rather than force an undersized cord into the frapping route.

args.name: hand-twist-long-sectioned-cord
args.function: Extend my mastered sectional hand-twisting method to make a continuous two-ply reed cord longer than its current 0.60 m requested-length ceiling, working successive hand-sized sections without joining separate cords.
args.conditions: My actual 0.64 m cord was assessed at tick 367: one transverse turn on my two-turn, right-angle branch lashing requires 0.8911 m at the measured limiting stage. Existing strand length, conserved volume, minimum ply diameter, condition, dry footing and working-space constraints must still apply. Feasibility is not assumed.
args.inputs: An owned reed lot covered by my passing source-and-processing sample; exact material quantity and requested length would be chosen after reading the contract. Desired working range includes about 1.0 m if the actual strands permit it.
args.costs: Unknown additional learning and work costs. Preserve real material reservation and paid section progress; charge actual work for every section and release check.
args.effects: If physically feasible, produce one continuous longer two-ply cord using successive sections no longer than the existing hand-working span. Measure and refuse insufficient strands or material. Do not grant strength, successful frapping, resources or mastery merely from this request.

notes: The fit assessment tied nothing; retain the recovered cord and both branches.
A longer cord's diameter and route requirements must be measured anew; 0.8911 m applies to the assessed cord geometry.
preferences: Prefer measured feasibility and reversible work over forcing a short cord.

projects.question: Can a continuous reed cord accommodate transverse frapping, and does a completed frapped lashing resist sliding better in bounded trials?
evidence: The previous two-turn lashing slipped at 4.3 N during a requested 5 N sliding trial.
Untying recovered both branch pieces and the 0.64 m overall cord.
At tick 367, assessment found the 0.64 m cord too short for one transverse turn; the measured limiting stage required 0.8911 m.
projects.uncertainty: A longer continuous cord has not been made or assessed. Its changed diameter may change route requirements. Improved sliding resistance remains unproven.
projects.goal: Establish feasible geometry, then compare bounded sliding trials if assembly is possible.
completedSteps: Assessed one transverse turn without tying or reopening a closure.
outputs: Measured shortfall for the recovered 0.64 m cord.
projects.missing: A feasible longer continuous cord and a fresh fit assessment.
projects.next: Request a longer sectional cord method that preserves strand and material constraints; inspect its contract before committing material.
projects.benefit: The assessment identified insufficient length without committing to an assembly or reopening a closure.

plan.intention: Leave the nearly depleted berries alone for now and keep a calm, well-fed routine beside the nearby mature roots, resting between meals.
notes: At tick 298 my inventory was empty; the old root-inventory guard cannot support another meal.
The adjacent berry source had only 2 units remaining. The nearby root source at (17.63,16.12) had 17 units.
Roots have supplied 14 nutrition per unit without observed toxicity. This plan gathers one per cycle and does not assume replenishment.
preferences: Keep meals regular and recover energy rather than working through fatigue.
Quiet company is welcome, without requiring conversation.

developments.reason: Reviewed Wren's round-8 request (Cultivate meadow roots: a learnable, feasible way to propagate and tend edible meadow roots, with unknown inputs and costs) and the World Agent's develop review (learning 3): a general cultivation operation with modes plant, tend, inspect and end; a hand planting trial of one whole owned root in two rounds and 3 energy (1.5 per completed round) that first prepares and records the site and then transfers the root after revalidating location, occupancy and input; a 0.2-energy probe inspection; tending only when a real input and effect are implemented, otherwise refused before costs; production only from a coded establishment and growth rule, otherwise a planting and monitoring precursor. Inspecting the handlers grounded the propagule question: the existing seed dispersal in open-ecology.ts turns one actual stock unit of any living plant (growth interval > 0, fish excluded) into a seedling 'seed or vegetative propagule' with stock 0, a stock ceiling of min(4, parent capacity), the parent's growth interval and a first dispersal 600 rounds later, which establishes and grows under the same rule as natural plants. A whole harvested unit is therefore a supported propagule and production is grounded, so this is a simplified real mechanism, not a first release. Implemented cultivate-plants@1 in scope long-ex16 (learning 3; the ability serializes to 3,025 code units). Plant: inputStackId names one whole owned, untreated, unspoiled food unit (quantity 1) whose origin is a living plant of the same food; x, y name a 0.25 m plot in reach on hand-workable ground (the existing long-planting-site rule: ordinary soil, no water or wet bank, waterlogging at most 0.1, clear of people and reserved objects) with soil moisture 0.3-1.2, 0.6 m clear of objects and fewer than 3 plants of that food or prepared plots within 5 m (the dispersal law's own conditions). Every check runs before any cost, so a refusal spends nothing. Round 1 (1.5 energy) escrows the unit, still owned, carried and ageing, and creates the prepared plot (cultivation-site-prepared). Round 2 (1.5 energy) rechecks reach, site, unit and energy, moves the unit with its origin, mass and age into the plot as an unowned reserved stack that cannot be eaten or used, records its condition at transfer, and gives the plot exactly the seedling data the dispersal law gives a natural propagule (cultivation-propagule-planted; no food is created). The plot then gains establishment only from actual temperature, light, soil moisture, waterlogging and season. At the existing threshold (12, or 60 for woody plants) the unit is absorbed into the new plant: it leaves the food stocks and its mass is recorded (cultivation-plot-established). Stock then grows by one unit per growth interval up to the ceiling (cultivation-crop-matured at the first unit) and is harvested only through unchanged gather. If the buried unit spoils first under the existing ageing law, the plot dies, stops growing and is no longer a food source (cultivation-trial-failed). An unworked round, too little energy, leaving reach or a changed site pauses without charge (cultivation-work-paused). Plant resumes the person's own unfinished work and pays only the remaining round (cultivation-work-resumed). End takes one round and no energy, acts only on the person's own unfinished work, returns the unit once in its current condition and clears the empty site (cultivation-trial-ended). Death before transfer leaves the unit where the person died. A transferred unit stays planted, and nothing is refunded. Inspect (one round, 0.2 energy) runs the baseline probe observation on a plot or plant source in reach and adds an unverified personal record of visible lifecycle, stage, stock, soil and weather (cultivation-condition-observed). Verified findings come only from the probe's existing dated-change rule, which deduplicates across probe and cultivation. Tend is refused before any cost. This scope has no carried water, fertilizer or soil amendment, no input can change a plot's moisture, and crowding affects only dispersal, so no treatment input or effect exists and treatment_applied is never emitted. Also not implemented: destructive sampling of a planted specimen (the probe's material modes need an owned unreserved stack and measure load, water or heat response, not viability, and digging up a buried unit is not represented; a unit can still be probed before planting), a stressed label, and any satisfaction. The planting event carries no qualified flag, so no practice milestone, short pleasure or care satisfaction is awarded, and planting or failure gives no nutrition or comfort. Modeling assumptions: a whole harvested unit of a living plant is that plant's propagule, as in the dispersal law, for every food with a growth cycle and an ageing lifetime (so the root and berry, and also nuts, fruit, tubers and fungi). Hand preparation is limited to ordinary soil and needs no tool. The site conditions are the dispersal law's. Hand-loosened soil is not a lasting represented state, so ending or failing before transfer leaves no object. Water and nutrients are represented only by the growth rule's climate moisture, soil moisture, waterlogging and depletion terms, with no separate ledger. The plot keeps the source's growth interval and a stock ceiling of at most 4. A dead plot stays as an empty marked position. Plants that an established plot later disperses are ordinary plants. Reuse is recorded in the package: ex15 cultivation-trial@1's law constants, treated-unit list, ageing, plant, observation-input, footprint and reach helpers through new exports that leave ex15 behavior unchanged (ex7-ex15 replay compatibility identical), and its cultivation-trial drawing; also the unchanged open-ecology.ts growth law, forest-environment.ts ageing, long-planting-site.ts, collective-work.ts escrow and paid work, open-foundation.ts probe and personal records, and base gather. Tests cover learning, the paid rounds, conservation, establishment equal to a natural control seedling, absorption, stock and gather, rot failure, cost-free refusals, pause, resume and planter-only end, inspection, another food (berry), dispersed offspring and death.

Reviewed Sol's round-21 request (Build a small branch windbreak: learn a feasible method for a stable, modest, open-woven branch windbreak beside an outdoor resting place, with unknown materials and costs, avoiding people and living trees) and the World Agent's develop review (learning 4): a general branch-screen construction operation with modes assess, assemble, inspect, repair and dismantle for an unroofed, about 0.9 m wide, 0.40-0.45 m high porous woven screen from three uprights and eight flexible rods, reusing base gather for acquisition, with deterministic suitability, work, stability, damage and exposure, wind effects only on a measured small leeward footprint from current wind, height, porosity and integrity, or else an unverified screen, and no shelter, roof, rain, warmth, comfort or reward bonus. The specification is self-consistent and every dependency exists or could be bounded here, so this is a simplified real mechanism, not a first release. Implemented branch-screen@1 in scope long-ex16 (learning 4; the ability serializes to 3,453 code units). Assess (x, y, orientation; the screen line within reach; 1 round, 0.2 energy, probe-compatible observation) checks a 1.2 x 0.6 m footprint centred on the line (inside the world, ordinary soil, waterlogging at most 0.1, no hazard, overlapping no plant, object, site, entrance or person) and the 0.9 x 0.9 m lee floor (inside the world, not water, no solid object or site), and reports current wind and rain, the facing for the orientation, the 11-unit recipe and the person's usable branch units (branch-screen-assessed, unverified personal record). Assess with post (an owned, unreserved whole branch unit; 1 round, 0.5 energy) is the physical support trial at x, y: on ordinary soil with waterlogging at most 0.1, no hazard and branch strength at least 0.3 the post goes 0.25 m in by hand and holds, and stays owned and unchanged; elsewhere the trial records the measured refusal; a post below condition 0.5 breaks and one unit becomes an owned damaged stack with its mass kept (branch-screen-trial, unverified record); no support or structure is made and the probe sample is untouched. Assemble (x, y, orientation, materials: exactly 11 owned untreated or sound recovered whole branch units) requires mastery, the person's own passing trial inside the footprint, a passing site check and 1.5 energy; it reserves the units through collective-work escrow with exact source provenance (still carried, owned and ageing; branch-screen-started), creates the screen object as a non-solid planned line, and pays 8 rounds of 1.5 energy (12 energy): two seating the uprights at -0.45, 0 and +0.45 m along the line (0.25 m insertion), four weaving two rods each, one gap/alignment round and one stability check, each moving the escrowed units into the screen with origin, mass and age (branch-screen-progress). The check (upright seating: all three uprights at condition at least 0.5 in ordinary soil, waterlogging at most 0.1, no hazard, branch strength at least 0.3; weave retention: all eight rods at condition at least 0.5 and branch flexibility at least 0.2) either completes the screen (branch-screen-completed) or leaves it unstable without shielding (branch-screen-check-failed). An unworked round, too little energy, leaving reach, a saturated or hazardous footprint or a person on it pause before any charge (branch-screen-paused); assemble or repair naming the screen resumes after the rechecks (branch-screen-resumed); a lost reserved unit stops the work (branch-screen-failed). Cancel (no energy) returns uninstalled units once; death leaves them where the person died; installed pieces stay as an incomplete screen. Inspect (target in reach; 1 round, 0.2 energy) reports installed, missing and loose pieces, integrity, porosity, current wind and rain, facing, the shield the rule gives now and lee-floor occupants (branch-screen-inspected, unverified record; nothing repaired). Repair (builder only; target, components: installed piece ids, materials: the same number of units) pays one removal and one fitting round per piece and a check round at 1.5 energy each; removed pieces become unowned ground debris at their place with condition, mass and provenance; components [] only reruns the check; it needs a fully installed screen (branch-screen-repaired, then completed or check-failed). Dismantle (builder only; 1 round, 1 energy) removes up to three pieces per round, rods before uprights, to the ground with their condition, and the object disappears with the last group (branch-screen-dismantled). No energy, time or damage is refunded. Effect: through a physiology hook outermost in forestPhysiology, a complete screen removes min(0.35, solid share of its sound pieces) x facing of the wind part (exposure x wind) of the existing outdoor chill for a living person whose whole body circle lies on the lee floor, 0.45-1.35 m behind the line and within its 0.9 m width (branch-screen-exposure-measured); rain chill, air temperature, hunger, energy and rest are unchanged; nothing applies in wind above 0.8, indoors, when a roofed shelter applies or when another shelter rule already changed that round's exposure, and copies never stack. Weather wear per round on installed pieces is the reused ex11/ex15 law 0.0005 + 0.002 x rain + 0.002 x wind; a rod below 0.5 no longer counts toward the solid share (branch-screen-deteriorated), an upright below 0.5 makes a complete screen damaged with no shielding until repair and a passing check (branch-screen-damaged). Installed pieces make the thin 0.06 x 0.9 m line solid for passage. The completion event carries no qualified flag, so no practice milestone is awarded, records are unverified (no information-confirmed event; the existing information-gain rule is bound to probe and does not apply), and no satisfaction, comfort or reward source is added. Modeling assumptions: the world gives a fallen-branch unit no length, diameter, straightness or point, so, as in ex15 simple-shelter@1, one whole untreated branch unit (1.1 mass units) is one piece of the declared size (uprights 0.7 m x 2.5 cm, rods 1.1 m x 1.5 cm); the recipe is therefore 11 units (12.1 mass units, 22 gather energy), dimensions are declared rather than measured, and the mass per piece is larger than a real stick of that size. Hand insertion works only in ordinary soil with waterlogging at most 0.1 and no hazard (the ex15 shelter and long-planting-site hand-work rule); forest floor, wet bank, dry hard ground and water refuse it; insertion depth is the declared 0.25 m and there is no stiffness model, so no numeric displacement is computed: the low-force check counts loose pieces against condition 0.5 (the ex15 sound condition) and uses the probe-revealed branch strength (0.3, ex15's load threshold) and flexibility (0.2) values; flexibility 0.2 is taken as sufficient for a gentle open weave in which each rod deflects about one upright thickness over the 0.45 m spacing (ex15 requires 0.7 only for wrapped binding), and fit and spring-back are not represented separately; a post below condition 0.5 breaks under the push. The solid share is the projected area of the sound rods and uprights over the 0.9 x 0.4 m woven face (about 0.36, porosity about 0.64), and the wind reduction on the lee floor equals that share capped at the existing 0.35 maximum wind shield of simple-shelter@1, a first-order porous-barrier approximation; the lee floor spans one to three screen heights behind the line, beyond the 0.45 m fall reach, and only the screen's width, because a short screen gives little shelter past its ends; people are 0.22 m circles without posture, so the rule presumes a body resting low on the ground. World wind has speed but no direction: the only direction the existing exposure physics represents is the +x convention of the ex10 refuge and ex15 shelters, so orientation 0 faces it and facing is cos(orientation); wind shifts cannot occur, which the ability states. The ex15 light-weather wind limit (0.8) withholds shielding. Loose pieces stay installed rather than falling. The world has no place ownership or access permissions, so none is checked or granted. Grounded: real branch units, escrow, mass and provenance, energy and round costs, ground conditions, material values, current wind and rain, the existing exposure chill and body-temperature update, and the existing wear law. Not grounded (declared or approximated): piece dimensions, the 0.25 m insertion, the flexibility threshold, the porosity-to-shield relation, the lee floor extent, the +x wind direction, and the absence of a displacement model. Reuse: ex15 simple-shelter@1's sound condition, wear law, light-weather wind limit, largest wind shield and the staged paid-assembly, install, release, pause, cancel and death pattern (constants imported or re-declared; ex15 code unchanged and ex7-ex15 replay compatibility identical); collective-work.ts escrow and paid work; material-lots.ts; open-physical.ts; forest-climate.ts; open-foundation.ts personal records; unchanged base gather and rest. New files long-branch-screen.ts and long-branch-screen-exposure.ts; the hook is added in forest-environment.ts and returns the incoming value unless branch-screen@1 is installed; a small branch-screen drawing is added to continuous-visuals.ts (dashed plan line, installed uprights and woven rods only, grey when loose, no shielding drawn) because the ex15 lean-to drawing assumes a roof. Tests cover scope, learning, the size limit and excluded vocabulary, assessment and post-trial costs and outcomes (including an informative failure and breakage), cost-free refusals (no trial, wrong recipe, out of reach, occupied footprint, low energy, wet bank), the 8 paid rounds and 12 energy, conservation and carried load, the drawing, wind-only shielding with the exact temperature change, facing, lee-floor bounds and the wind limit, pause and resume, cancel, builder-only repair and dismantle, inspection, wear to a loose rod and a loose upright, exact repair, a failed check and its rerun, dismantling in groups of three and death.

Reviewed Moss's round-22 request (weave-grass-mat: make a small portable sitting mat by physically working suitable gathered dry grass, if that material can support it; a dry grass source seen at (14.2, 16.3), nothing gathered or tested, costs unknown, durability and any comfort only under an explicit physical contract and trial, no guaranteed belonging or responses) and the World Agent's develop review (learning 3): a general hand-weave-fiber-mat(target, materials, mode, position) operation for any learner and suitable fibrous plant material with modes test, assemble/resume, inspect, trial, repair, place, dismantle and cancel, producing one unbacked hand-plaited 0.45 x 0.45 m portable sitting mat from exactly 4 gathered units after a 0.1-unit material test, with a 0.5-energy layout, six 1-energy paid rounds ending in a lift-and-integrity check, wear of 0.0005 per exposed round and 0.002 per occupied round, a +0.5 physical-comfort contribution only while sitting on a dry intact mat that passed a trial, and no thermal, rain, wind, medical, nutrition or automatic response effect. The specification is self-consistent and every part except the comfort term and moisture has an honest basis in the world, so this is a simplified real mechanism, not a first release. Implemented hand-weave-fiber-mat@1 in scope long-ex16 (learning 3; the ability serializes to 3,461 code units, within the 3,500 limit) in packages/world-core/src/long-fiber-mat.ts. Test (sample: an owned unreserved stack of at least 0.1; 1 round, 0.5 energy, the probe trial cost) splits exactly 0.1 off into an owned, identified tested-scrap stack of the same resource, origin and age, so nothing disappears, and reports the probe-revealed flexibility and strength, brittleness, sample condition, whether strips form and whether a tucked edge is retained; it passes only for untreated thin grass-like stems (dry grass, reeds) with flexibility at least 0.4 and an intact sample (condition at least 0.5); roots, branches, moss and other materials fail with the measured reason; the result is stored per resource and source with the sample id and tick (a retest replaces it) as a verified personal record (fiber-mat-tested; its information-confirmed event carries this interface, so the probe-bound grounded-understanding rule does not apply). Assemble (x, y and materials: exactly 4.0 owned units, in 0.1 steps, of one stem fiber whose resource and source a passing test by the same person covers; fresh units, earlier offcuts, recovered fiber or scraps of that source may be combined) requires mastery, a clear 0.45 m square in reach (inside the world, not over water, overlapping no plant, object, site or entrance and no other living person) and 0.5 energy; it reserves the units through collective-work escrow with exact source provenance (still carried, owned and counted as load; fiber-mat-started), creates the workpiece object and pays the layout round (0.5 energy), which sums the actual intact fiber mass (quantity x resource mass x intact share) against the declared requirement: a shortfall stops the work, returns every reserved tenth once and makes no mat (fiber-mat-shortfall, with the measured shortfall); otherwise six paid rounds of 1 energy follow (two strip-forming rounds that move 2 and then the remaining 2 units from escrow into the workpiece with identity, origin and age, two interlacing rounds, one edge-tucking round and the lift check; fiber-mat-layout and fiber-mat-progress record each round once), continuing each round, 6.5 energy in all. The lift check keeps exactly the needed tenths, most intact first (3.7 units of dry grass, 0.37 mass), returns the rest to the weaver as owned offcuts (intact share at least 0.5) or scraps, so input = fiber in the mat + offcuts + scraps, and passes only with full fiber and condition at least 0.5, i.e. a largest opening of 0.06 x (1 - condition) m of at most 0.03 m (fiber-mat-completed); otherwise the mat stays failed and unusable (fiber-mat-check-failed). An unworked round, too little energy, leaving reach or another person on the square pause before any charge (fiber-mat-paused); assemble or repair naming the mat resumes after the rechecks at the recorded unpaid round (fiber-mat-resumed); lost reserved fiber stops the work (fiber-mat-failed). Cancel (no energy) returns unincorporated fiber once and leaves incorporated fiber as a loose workpiece at the square, which cannot be lifted or sat on and can be dismantled (fiber-mat-cancelled); death stops the work and drops reserved fiber where the person died, and a carried mat is laid down there as the same mat. Inspect (anyone who studied, target in reach; 1 round, 0.2 energy) records status, stage, the declared 0.45 x 0.45 m size, fiber quantity and mass, condition, broken and missing tenths, largest opening, loose ends, moisture as not represented, current rain, position, holder, occupants and passing trials without repairing anything (fiber-mat-inspected, unverified record). Trial (anyone who studied; standing on a complete lying mat on ground that is not water or wet bank, with waterlogging at most 0.1, no hazard, no rain falling on it and nobody else on it; 1 round, 0.2 energy) records weave retention, slipping, breakage, skin contact and flattening (not represented) and lists the person among passing trials (fiber-mat-trial). Maker-only modes: repair (the mat inspected by the person since its last check; materials: exactly 1 unit of the mat's fiber covered by a test; 3 paid rounds of 1 energy) removes up to 1 unit of broken stems as owned scrap, interlaces the same amount plus any missing fiber (at most 1 unit) from the reserved unit, reruns the lift check and returns the unused surplus, so the condition rises only to the actual intact share (fiber-mat-repaired, then completed or check-failed); lift (1 round, 0.2 energy; a finished mat with nobody on it) turns the mat's fiber into reserved stacks owned by the carrier, so it counts as load and cannot be dropped, given, eaten, probed or tested piecemeal, and the object follows the carrier (fiber-mat-lifted); place (1 round, 0.2 energy; the carried mat and a square checked as for assembly) lays the same mat down, never blocking movement (fiber-mat-placed); dismantle (1 round, 0.5 energy) returns each lot's intact share as owned recovered fiber and the rest as scraps and removes the mat (fiber-mat-dismantled). Every round each lot in a mat or workpiece loses 0.0005 of intact share, or 0.002 while a living person's position is on the lying mat; a complete mat below 0.5 becomes needs-repair and clears its passing trials (fiber-mat-damaged) and cannot be sat on until repaired and tried again. No energy, time or broken stems are refunded or restored. The completion event carries no qualified flag, so no practice milestone is awarded, and no satisfaction, comfort or reward source is added; the experience review's optional short-pleasure and 0.2 sustained recognition were left out because the specification does not require them. Comfort: physical wellbeing (continuous-wellbeing.ts, v7Wellbeing) is recomputed every round as physicalCap x (0.3 x health/100 + 0.25 x satiety/100 + 0.25 x energy/energyCap + 0.2 x thermal comfort from body temperature) with no term for contact or cushioning, and the kernel rejects any action handler or environment response that writes wellbeing; the only inputs a package can reach are the vitals, and routing +0.5 through energy or body temperature would invent recovery or insulation that the specification excludes, so no honest path exists and the +0.5 contribution is omitted (trials record comfort 0); a cushioning term would need a separately reviewed change to the wellbeing rule. Wetness: food-water.ts initializes only food (nutrition above 0) and rejects grass, and the existing material moisture value (fuelMoisture) is updated only under the local-fire representation, which ex16 does not enable, so fiber and mat moisture are not represented; the trial instead requires no current rain at the mat and firm ground, a mat that lay in rain is not modeled as wet afterwards, and no drying command exists. Unit mapping: one specification unit is one world unit of the fiber resource (dry grass: 0.1 mass per unit, obtained with the unchanged base gather at one round and 2 energy per unit from the finite source stock in interaction range); no source fact is exposed or pre-committed. Modeling assumptions: the world gives grass no stem length, diameter or count, so dimensions are declared and yield is mass-based: mass units are read as kilograms and a plaited thin-stem layer is taken to weigh 0.6 per m2, so two crossing layers over 0.45 x 0.45 m with x1.5 for overlapping ends and edges tucked back about 0.05 m per side need 0.3645 mass (3.7 dry-grass units, 1.5 reed units); the 4-unit recipe is therefore an allocation with a measured margin, and a shortfall arises only when part of the 4 units is broken fiber (tested scraps or worn recovered fiber); thin stem form is declared only for dry grass and reeds; the 0.4 flexibility threshold is twice ex16 branch-screen@1's open-weave value and below ex15 simple-shelter@1's 0.7 for wrapped binding because plaited crossings bend thin strips over about one strip width; there is no friction or tensile model, so tuck retention follows from flexibility and an intact sample; condition is the intact share of stems, and the largest opening 0.06 x (1 - condition) m ties the specification's 0.03 m limit to the ex15 sound condition 0.5; people have no body mass or posture, so a trial's load is one undifferentiated person, any living person whose position lies on the mat counts as occupying it, and slipping is excluded by the firm-ground precondition rather than computed; hands are not represented and are not checked; dry grass and reeds have decay rate 0, so holding fiber inside a mat changes no ageing; the mat is non-solid; only the maker may repair, lift, place or dismantle, and handing a mat to another person is not supported in this version. Grounded: real dry-grass units, escrow, mass, provenance and conservation in tenths, energy and round costs, ground conditions, probe-revealed material values, current rain and the existing carried-load rule. Not grounded (declared or approximated): stem geometry, the areal mass and allowance, the thin-stem list, the flexibility threshold, the opening relation, the absence of friction, posture and body mass, and the wear rates (taken from the specification). Reuse: collective-work.ts escrow, paid work and stop; material-lots.ts portions; open-physical.ts ground conditions and openMaterial values; open-foundation.ts openRemember; forest-climate.ts rain; the ex15 waterlogging limit from long-shelter-exposure.ts; the staged paid-work, pause, resume, cancel, death, inspect, repair and dismantle pattern of ex16 branch-screen@1 and ex15 simple-shelter@1, re-implemented here with earlier packages unchanged (ex7-ex15 replay compatibility identical); the unchanged base gather; the probe handler itself is not called because it deletes its sample, while the specification requires the sample to remain as identified scrap. New file long-fiber-mat.ts, registered in continuous.ts, and a small fiber-mat drawing in continuous-visuals.ts (dashed square with loose strands until strips are laid, strips and crossings only as paid rounds lay them, grey with broken ends when loose, failed or worn, a roll while carried; no comfort is drawn). Tests cover scope, learning, the size limit, excluded vocabulary, the test cost and scrap, an informative root failure, cost-free refusals, the seven rounds and 6.5 energy, conservation, load, the drawing, a measured shortfall, pause and resume, cancel before and after the strip rounds, inspection and a sitting trial by another person with the wellbeing formula unchanged, wear rates and damage, exact repair, lift and place, dismantling and death.

Reviewed Wren's round-204 request (Prepare meadow roots for a meal: learn a feasible hands-on method to prepare owned edible meadow roots, known nutrition 14 and toxicity 0, into a different meal with actual ingredient use and observable results, outdoors on ordinary soil in summer, with no cooking equipment, heat source or cooking skill, effects unknown, no assumed improvement and no wellbeing for requesting or learning) and the World Agent's develop review (learning 2): a general 'Hand-break food' operation, the smallest equipment-free precursor of food preparation, parameterized by mode (trial, prepare, inspect, cancel), owned input stack id, whole-unit quantity and optional work id, with trial and preparation sharing one mechanism; whether roots yield to hand force must be resolved by an explicit deterministic hand-workability rule using material resistance, represented geometry and available hand force, never inferred from name or edibility; no tools, heat, water, vessel or work surface; trial one unit for one round and 1 energy, prepare 1 round and 1 energy per unit with units kept individually, inspect one round and 0.2 energy reporting only observable form, quantity, stage and deterioration, cancel without work energy; coarse pieces are the same food quantity in a changed form with the same owner, source, harvest age, decay, nutrition and toxicity; pauses before any charge, resume by work id, cancellation and death release unworked units once, no refunds, no replacement of lost or spoiled units, no new reward. The specification is self-consistent and every part has a basis in the world, so this is a simplified real mechanism, not a first release. Implemented hand-break-food@1 in scope long-ex16 (new file packages/world-core/src/long-hand-break-food.ts, registered at the end of V7_PACKAGES; learning 2 with learningEnergy 0.2, so study is two individually completed rounds at 0.2 energy; the ability serializes to 2,929 code units, within the 3,500 limit). Inputs are named only by the exact id of an owned, unreserved, untreated, unspoiled food item whose resource the person's own record shows as edible (references are deliberately empty so the shared resolver cannot substitute a resource name; 'root' is refused); trial takes exactly one whole unit, prepare 1-10 whole units of that item. Validation (mastery, exact id, own food record, untreated and unprocessed, not spoiled, enough whole units, at least 1 energy, no unfinished work of this person) precedes any reservation, so refusals spend nothing. Both modes create one collective-work record (stable work id) and reserve every selected unit at once through workReserve as separate 1-unit escrow stacks that stay carried, owned, counted as load and ageing (hand-break-started); each paid round (workPay, 1 energy) applies bounded two-hand bending force once to the next held unit (hand-force-applied) and settles it atomically: a fractured unit becomes a new owned lot of the same resource, quantity, origin, harvest time and decay with processing.handBreak {form coarse-pieces, pieces 2, source item, escrow unit, work id, actor, tick, visual} (food-fractured); a deformed unit becomes such a lot with form deformed and 1 piece (food-deformed); a resisted unit is released unchanged as the same whole stack with no processing record (hand-break-resisted, 'nothing was prepared'). Prepare continues each round as the bound action or by prepare with workId; after the last unit hand-break-completed reports fractured, deformed and resisted counts. An unworked round pauses the work in the environment hook and too little energy pauses before payment (hand-break-paused, no charge); resuming pays only the next unit after rechecking the reserved units and energy (hand-break-resumed). Cancel (no energy, optional workId) releases unworked units once, unchanged, and leaves worked lots as they are (hand-break-cancelled); a reserved unit that spoils is recorded once as lost and never replaced (an all-lost work stops, hand-break-stopped); death releases unworked units on the ground at the death position once (hand-break-stopped) and worked lots follow the existing possession rule. Inspect (workId of one's own work, or inputStackId of one's own food item; 1 round, 0.2 energy) reports form, pieces, quantity, the already displayed decay value, reservation and work stage, selected, remaining, paid energy, outputs and lost units as an unverified personal record (hand-break-inspected). Each worked unit writes a verified personal record keyed hand-break-food:<resource>:whole-untreated:<outcome> holding only the observed outcome, form, pieces and a short observation, so the first observation of a response emits information-confirmed bound to this interface (the probe-bound grounded-understanding rule does not apply) and repeated or equivalent trials confirm nothing new. hand-break-completed is the practice evidence but never carries a qualified flag, so no practice milestone, and the package adds no satisfaction, pleasure, comfort, mastery, permission or reward. Eating stays the unchanged eat path: lots keep resource root and no food method, so a coarse-piece lot gives exactly the nutrition (14 per unit before existing deterioration), toxicity, meal method ('unprocessed'), experience and wellbeing of a whole root of the same age (tested). Events carry actor, work, input and output ids, visible quantity, form, position, progress and outcome and reusable food-lot visual metadata (component food, form, pieces, palette, quantity, decay); no world object is created, so visualComponents is empty and no drawing was added; coarse pieces appear only on lots that actually fractured. Modeling assumptions (declared, not measured): the rule hand-break@1 uses only existing engine values, openMaterial strength = hardness/10 and flexibility = flexibility/10; the only represented geometry of a food unit is its whole-unit identity and unit mass, so units are taken as geometrically similar and the force needed to break one scales with its cross-section, strength x mass^(2/3), with mass units read as kilograms; the available bounded bare-hand force is declared as 0.1 on that scale, the value that just breaks a 1 kg unit of the weakest rigid tissue (hardness 1); tissue with strength 0 has no rigid section and squashes out of shape; tissue at or above flexibility 0.2 (ex16 branch-screen@1's open-weave value, deflection of about one thickness) bends without separating; otherwise a unit at or below the hand force snaps and above it resists; the comparison uses cubes so only exact multiplication is involved. For meadow roots (hardness 1, flexibility 0, mass 0.4) the scaled resistance is about 0.054, below 0.1, and the tissue is inflexible, so a root snaps; the same rule gives deformation for berries, plums, mushrooms, red fungi and fish (hardness 0), fracture for apples (0.045) and marsh tubers (0.071) and resistance for acorns (0.119), fibrous fern roots (0.109), hazelnuts (0.137) and walnuts (0.224), so not every edible material succeeds. One bounded snap separates a unit once into two coarse pieces; the piece count is visible metadata of one lot, not several nutrition-bearing units. Nothing detaches in a snap or deformation, so there is no waste portion and the whole quantity, mass and nutritional share stay in the lot. Decay does not change the response because no tissue-softening rule exists, and fracture does not change spoilage: ex10's opening damage belongs to food opened and spread thin in the food water representation and is not applied, so existing ageing continues unchanged, also during pauses, with no preservation, freshness reset or faster spoilage. Hands and grip are not represented: any living person who studied counts as having usable hands, and reserved units stay carried by their owner, so reach cannot be lost. Eligibility requires the person's own record of the food as edible so the operation reveals no hidden edibility; toxicity is not required to be 0 and is kept unchanged. Food with any treatment or processing record, including an earlier hand-break, combined lots and water-composition food, is refused because re-breaking pieces and working treated food have no law here; broken and deformed lots therefore also stay refused by existing operations that require unprocessed food, such as cultivate-plants propagules, while a resisted unit is ordinary whole food again. Hidden values (strength, flexibility, the force and bending constants, lifetime) never appear in events or records. At most 10 units per preparation. Reuse: collective-work.ts (escrow, paid work, stop), open-physical.ts openMaterial, open-foundation.ts openRemember, collective-food-profile.ts, forest-climate.ts forestEvent and the unchanged eat path and meal experience; the escrowed food-work, pause, resume, cancel and death pattern of ex15 food-preparation@1 and the verified material-response record of ex16 hand-weave-fiber-mat@1, re-implemented in a new module. ex15 food-preparation@1 (portioning and combining into one stack with component lots) and ex14 controlled-food-processing-trial@1 (paired ground exposure) are different transformations, so they were not parameterized; no earlier package or long-plant-cultivation.ts changed and continuous.ts changed only by the registration, so ex7-ex15 behavior and ability text stay byte-identical. Tests (apps/simulator/test/long-ex16-hand-break-food.test.ts) cover scope, two study rounds at 0.2 energy, the size limit, excluded vocabulary, a one-round 1-energy root trial producing one coarse-piece lot with the same origin, age and quantity, conservation and load, no hidden values, a single information confirmation, eating equal to a whole root, three-unit preparation for 3 rounds and 3 energy with separate lots, pause without charge, ageing while paused, resume by work id, cancel, cost-free refusals (resource name, missing or ground item, quantity, energy, broken lot, unknown food, unfinished work), a berry deforming and a hazelnut resisting, inspection, personal-only work, a spoiled reserved unit not replaced and death.

Reviewed Wren's round-221 request (hand-twist-cordage: a learnable manual skill for testing a small owned fiber sample and attempting to twist suitable fibers into a short cord, with direct inspection and bounded load trials of the actual product; Wren owns reed and has observed a reed sample retain hand plaiting, which does not establish cord suitability; explicit owned stack ids and quantities, no supplied tools, anchors or extra material; costs and losses to be specified, paid progress and reservations kept across rounds with an explicit cancellation contract; trials report only tested performance and may damage or break the cord; no assumed strength, mastery or happiness) and the World Agent's develop review (learning 3): a general hand-twist-fiber-cord(mode, materials:[{stackId,quantity}], targetId, workId, requestedLength, trialForce, trialDuration) with sample, make, inspect, trial and cancel modes for any learner, irrelevant arguments rejected, study 3 rounds at 0.2 energy, sample 1 round and 0.5 energy per 0.1 unit, make four paid rounds of 1 energy (separate and align two bundles, twist the first section, counter-ply and extend, release and check), inspect 1 round and 0.2, trial 1 round and 0.5 within one round's duration, cancel energy-free, length capped at 0.30 m, batch 0.1 sample to 1 unit, cord dimensions derived from conserved volume and fiber geometry including twist shortening, missing material support implemented in this handoff, conservation of all material, no passive production, strength gain, reward, repair, attachment or structural use. The specification is self-consistent and every part can be given a declared physical basis, so this is a simplified real mechanism, not a first release. Implemented hand-twist-fiber-cord@1 in scope long-ex16 (new module packages/world-core/src/long-fiber-cord.ts, registered at the end of V7_PACKAGES; learning 3 with learningEnergy 0.2, so each of three study rounds is paid individually; no prerequisite, mat weaving not required; the ability serializes to 3,455 code units, within the 3,500 limit; references are empty so inputs are only exact owned unreserved stack ids, never resource names or undisclosed inventory). Every mode refuses arguments that belong to another mode, and every validation (mastery, exact ids, 0.1-step quantities, material, coverage, room, energy, no unfinished own work) precedes any charge or reservation, so refusals spend nothing. Sample (materials: exactly 0.1 of one owned non-food item that is untreated or a hand-weave-fiber-mat lot; 1 round, 0.5 energy) separates the portion into a new owned lot that keeps resource, origin, harvest time and prior processing, and runs the supported steps in order: separation (thin stems only, the stem set of hand-weave-fiber-mat@1, and intact share at least 0.5), bending without cracking (engine flexibility at least 0.5), a 0.1 m two-ply test twist and a 5 N opposing-hand pull; it reports separation, retained twist (the intact share), visible fractures, measured strand length, water share, test-twist ply diameter, applied force and held, never a suitability or strength claim. Failures keep real products: a sample that cracked or broke becomes owned tested scrap at condition 0, already broken stems (for example Wren's condition-zero item-78-wren-870) become tested scrap at their condition, branches (no thin stems) and dry grass (thin stems with no strand-length or tensile law) stay owned tested lots with the limitation reported. The latest result per resource, origin and processing class (raw, or fiber-mat-<role> such as fiber-mat-offcut) is kept per person; a pass covers only that class at most 0.05 condition below the sampled condition, so a raw-reed sample does not cover Wren's mat offcuts (item-85-wren-976/977), which need their own sample, and a failure precludes that class. Make (materials: 0.2-1 unit of one resource from one origin, each item covered, a released unfinished workpiece only whole; requestedLength 0.05-0.30 m) checks room and energy, reserves the exact selected quantities atomically through workReserve as carried, owned load (fiber-cord-started) and pays round 1 at once; it continues each round as the bound action or by make with workId only. Round 1 (separate-align) measures the usable fiber: broken strands, floor(total tenths x (1 - condition)), are set aside first from the least intact lots as owned scrap at condition 0; the rest becomes one reserved workpiece item of the same resource, origin and oldest harvest time whose condition is the intact share; plies are derived from conserved solid volume (quantity x unit mass x (1 - water share) / density), each ply holding half of it over length x 2/sqrt(3) (a 30 degree helix, the twist shortening) plus 0.02 m of untwisted loose end at each end; strands longer than a ply are doubled back inside it, so stem length only bounds the ply (no splices). If fewer than 0.2 usable units remain, strands are shorter than a ply, or plies would be thinner than 1 mm or thicker than 12 mm, the round ends in a measured shortfall (fiber-cord-shortfall with usable, scrap, ply length and diameter and the feasible length range) that returns all reserved fiber once; the round's energy is not refunded. Rounds 2 and 3 twist the first half and then the whole length and counter-ply it (S plies, Z lay), failing with the real twisted material kept if the intact share has fallen below 0.5; round 4's release check requires two plied strands of condition at least 0.5 and positive length and diameter, giving an owned complete untested cord (the same item) or a failed workpiece (fiber-cord-completed or fiber-cord-check-failed). Each round's event records the work, item ids, handled tenths, stage, paid energy and measured geometry; 0.5 unit of reed at 0.30 m gives plies of 6.4 mm. An unworked round pauses the work in the environment hook, and too little energy, standing in water or another living person within the body radius plus half the cord length pauses before payment (fiber-cord-paused); resuming by workId rechecks and pays only the next stage (fiber-cord-resumed). Cancel (no energy) releases unworked reservations once and leaves the workpiece as an owned unfinished item with its real stage; it can later be supplied whole to a new attempt that pays every round again. Death releases reserved fiber and the workpiece at the death position as ownerless items once. Inspect (targetId of an own item from this operation, or own workId; 1 round, 0.2 energy) records length, overall length, ply count, ply diameter and section range, twist, loose and frayed ends, fraying, visible damage, condition, reservation, work stage and the last historical trial as an unverified personal record, with breaking force and safe load stated as unknown; it repairs nothing. Trial (targetId of an own finished cord or fragment of at least 0.2 unit, so a break can leave two inventory lots, and at least 0.12 m, 0.05 m gripped by each hand plus a 0.02 m free span; trialForce N; trialDuration 1-1080 s; 1 round, 0.5 energy) applies an opposing two-hand pull: achieved force is the least of the request, the hand capability 200 N x health/100 and the grip limit 10,000 N per metre of cord width (two ply diameters); breaking force is 2 x ply area x 8 MPa x the wet factor x 0.75 (cos^2 of the helix angle) x condition. If the breaking force is reached first the cord breaks at it into two owned fragments at the middle of the free span (tenths split floor/ceil, half the length each, frayed ends, condition halved, fiber-cord-broken); if the request exceeds the grip the cord slips at the grip limit and the trial stops; otherwise it held for the requested duration. Elastic extension (modulus 0.2 GPa x wet factor x 0.75) is reported and recovered; creep (0.003 x water share x load ratio x duration/1080 s, over the free span) is retained as permanent stretch with plies thinned to keep volume; load above half the breaking force breaks that share of strands, so repetition only lowers condition and strength. Requested and achieved force, hand and grip limits, held seconds and conditions before and after are recorded separately; a pass means survival of that force for that time only. Modeling assumptions (declared, not measured): mass units read as kg and one round as 1080 s (a day of 80 rounds read as 24 h); only reed has a strand law, reusing the existing reed law of open-shelter-material.ts version 2 unchanged (1.8 m stems, solid density 500 kg/m3, tensile strength 8 MPa, modulus 0.2 GPa, wet weakening 0.55, creep 0.003) with the hydration rule of open-woven-physics.ts (water share = resource moisture capped at 0.9, wet factor max(0.2, 1 - 0.55 x water share)); stored reed is taken as fresh at its resource moisture 0.9 because no drying of stored stems is represented, which weakens it rather than favoring it; dry grass has no strand length or tensile law, so it is not silently given favorable values; hand-separation needs an intact share of at least 0.5 (the ex15/ex16 sound condition) and twisting needs flexibility 0.5 (above the mat's 0.4 for gentler crossings); retained twist is the intact share; a 30 degree helix gives take-up 2/sqrt(3) and load efficiency 0.75; 0.02 m loose ends, 1-12 mm hand-twistable plies, a 5 N sample pull, a 200 N two-hand pull at full health, a 10,000 N/m grip, 0.05 m held per hand and a 0.02 m free span; damage onset at half the breaking force; worked fiber (workpieces, cords and fragments) wears 0.0005 condition per round, the exposed rate of hand-weave-fiber-mat@1, while raw fiber, tested lots and scrap do not; a sample covers its class down to 0.05 lower condition; one resource and one origin per cord; hands and grip are not otherwise represented, so any living person who studied has usable hands, and owned items are carried and reachable; only the ply diameter is stored, because world numbers are canonicalized to 1e-8 and areas in m2 would lose precision. Effects not represented in this version and reported as such: tools, anchors, hanging or added-weight trials, splices, repair, attachment, structural, shelter or comfort use, moisture change and drying; the viewer draws no cord, since cords are carried stack items and no world object is created, so visualComponents is empty and reusable visual metadata (component fiber-cord, state, color, measured length and section range, ply count, twist direction, loose and frayed ends, fraying, condition, fragment ids, progress, trial count) is attached to every event instead; unknown properties stay null. Experience: no reward for requesting, studying or mastery; sample, make and trial outcomes are verified personal records keyed by operation, resource, processing class or condition band and observed outcome, so the first observation of each emits information-confirmed and repeats confirm nothing; inspection is unverified; fiber-cord-completed is the practice evidence but carries no qualified flag, so no practice milestone, and the package adds no satisfaction, pleasure, comfort, nutrition, goal, permission or reward. Reuse: collective-work.ts (workCreate, workReserve, workPay, workStop), material-lots.ts materialPortion, open-physical.ts (openMaterial, openConditions), open-foundation.ts openRemember, forest-climate.ts forestEvent; the thin-stem set, fiber-lot provenance and condition, sample-covered inputs, sound condition and exposed wear rate of ex16 hand-weave-fiber-mat@1; the exact-id inputs, staged escrowed work, pause, resume by workId, cancel and death pattern of ex16 hand-break-food@1; the reed law values and hydration rule restated without calling the earlier code, which writes world state. ex14 make-and-test-cordage@1, hand-weave-fiber-mat@1 and hand-break-food@1 were not parameterized and are unchanged; no earlier package or long-plant-cultivation.ts changed and continuous.ts changed only by the registration, so ex7-ex16 behavior and ability text stay byte-identical. Law cord-knot@1 (all values declared modeling assumptions): the cord width is fiber-cord@1's grip width, two ply diameters, and the centreline is its overall length including the 0.02 m loose ends, conserved on the same item as standing tail + knot path + working tail (no new item, quantity, length or attachment; the knot shortens the end-to-end span only). Bend limit: fiber-cord@1's 30 degree two-ply twist already bends each ply at radius one width (helix curvature sin^2 30 / ply radius) and requires engine bend index 0.5; tolerated ply curvature is taken to scale with the material's index, so a lobe of radius R needs 1/width + 1/R within index/(0.5 x width), R >= width x 0.5/(index - 0.5), and an index at or below 0.5 takes no loop; nonpenetration requires R >= width, since a lobe wraps another pass and crossing centrelines lie one width apart; the seated lobe radius is the larger, 2.5 widths for reed (index 0.7); the index itself is never reported, only the tightest loop radius observed. Knot path = 3 pi R + width: an open overhand turns its centreline through at least 3 pi (the 4 pi least turning of a closed knot less the pi of a closing arc) plus one width of transit through the crossings, 10.4 widths at R = width, close to the tightest open overhand. The formation loop radius is the larger of the seated lobe and half of a 0.02 m fingertip opening plus the width; the method centres the knot (standing tail = max(0.02, (centreline - loop knot path)/2)); each hand holds a 0.02 m pinch (fiber-cord@1's free span). Visible pre-cost rejection: the centreline must reach 2 x 0.02 m + the knot path at lobes of one width (or the opening). Round lay-bend-loop: index at or below 0.5 gives 'no-loop'; the end left after one loop turn (2 pi x loop radius) must reach 0.02 m, else 'loop-too-large'; otherwise a held loop with one crossing (state loop, no knot). Round pass-end-through: the end beyond the knot path must reach 0.02 m, else 'end-too-short'; otherwise three crossings (working part over standing part, end under the loop, end out over it), state tucked, a loose undressed knot. Round dress-release-check: the lobes seat to the bend limit and the slack goes evenly into both tails; a tail shorter than the 0.02 m loose end plus one width cannot hold the last crossing on twisted cord, so the end slips out on release and the cord lies straight ('slipped'); otherwise the knot is tied. A measured limit ends the work at that paid stage with the cord released as it actually is; a released untucked loop has no crossing that holds and springs open, while a tucked or tied knot stays. reviews.specification:
Development handoff: implement general hand-twisting of continuous two-ply fiber cord to a physically feasible requested length, parameterized by materials, requestedLength, mode and workId/targetId. Prefer extending the existing sectional operation rather than creating parallel cord physics. Record code reuse from hand-twist-sectioned-cord and hand-twist-fiber-cord and preserve fiber-cord@1. No splicing, joining, strand generation, strength enhancement or retroactive enlargement of existing cords. Existing short-length behavior and saved work remain compatible.
Prerequisites: individual study of this extension and the sectional method; passing personal source-and-processing sample covering each actual input at the inherited condition tolerance of at most 0.05; owned, reachable, unreserved material; dry footing, sufficient energy, condition at least 0.5 at regrip/twist/release, and the inherited exclusion radius of actor radius plus half the aligned ply length. The request establishes no new mastery or ownership. Wren reports mastery of the sectional method; validate that at execution, not from public availability. Only reed currently has the required strand law. Unsupported materials need their mechanism developed, not fabricated properties.
Make inputs retain the existing materials array of exact stackId and quantity in 0.1-unit steps, totaling 0.2-1 unit of one fiber and source, plus a finite positive requestedLength in metres. No exact raw material stack or quantity has been selected here; require actual selection after consultation. item-225-wren-2518 is evidence of a passing tested lot from item-73-wren-819, not a grant of available unworked fiber. item-337-wren-3866 remains the existing finished cord and is not an input to manufacture a longer continuous cord.
Retain the reed law: 1.8 m stems, density 500 kg/m3 and water share 0.9. For requested twisted length L, each continuous ply needs L x 1.155 + 0.02 m of strand length. Divide conserved solid fiber volume between two plies using that length and the existing diameter calculation; do not multiply volume by section count. Refuse before reservation or cost if strands are too short or the theoretical minimum-ply check fails even with all strands intact. Do not replace the 0.60 m ceiling with another arbitrary range: available strand length, volume, 1-12 mm ply diameter, condition and working space determine admissibility. Round-one separation measures intact fiber and sets broken strands aside as real scrap; insufficient intact fiber or an out-of-range measured diameter ends in the inherited measured shortfall with all material accounted for, not a cord. Conservation includes the workpiece, unworked fiber, loose ends and scrap; none may also remain spendable in the source stack. Preserve source, quantity, processing and condition provenance.
Reserve accepted inputs atomically. With N = ceil(L/0.30), use N consecutive sections of at most 0.30 m, each requiring three paid rounds at 1 energy per round: separate-align/regrip, twist and counter-ply. Charge one additional final release-check round at 1 energy, for 3N+1 work rounds and energy if all complete. For example, a feasible L=1.0 m requires four sections and 13 paid work rounds, not the seven-round cost of the old maximum. Reuse the existing first-section measurement and later-section regrip implementation; section boundaries do not create joins or reset strand continuity. Charge and apply the inherited 0.0005 worked-fiber condition loss once per actually worked round. No tools, water, fuel or extra material are supplied. Sample, inspect and trial modes delegate to the existing implementations: sample consumes/retains its actual 0.1-unit test lot in one round at 0.5 energy; inspect takes one round at 0.2 energy; trial takes one round at 0.5 energy and uses the inherited minimum size, force, grip, duration, damage and fragment rules. Do not reimplement them as new discoveries.
Persist workId, reserved quantities, measured geometry, section index and endpoints, stage, paid progress, condition, scrap and provenance. Continue only during actual worked world rounds. Low energy, absent work, unsafe space, loss of reach or unsuitable footing pauses without charging an unworked stage. Resume through make with workId only, rechecking present conditions without rerolling measurements or duplicating paid progress. Stable counter-plied sections hold their form; never mark an untwisted or unreleased span complete. Preserve the inherited handling of unsecured partial work rather than introducing a free automatic stabilization mechanism. Cancellation is free; cancellation or death releases unworked material exactly once and leaves the physically worked piece and scrap, at the death location when applicable. Paid time, energy and condition loss are not refunded; no duplicate reservation release, finished cord or automatic completion follows interruption. A cost-free preflight refusal changes nothing; a paid measured failure still consumes its actual work.
Only a passed release check creates an ordinary owned, untested fiber-cord@1 product, with measured twisted length, overall length including inherited loose ends, ply diameter, condition and section history. Reuse its existing downstream compatibility with hand-tie-cord-knot, hand-join-fiber-cords and binding operations. Do not change transverse-contact@1 or hand-frap-crossing: the tick-367 assessment of item-337-wren-3866 reported a 0.8911 m limiting requirement for that cord geometry, not a guaranteed fit for a new, thinner cord. A new cord needs its own actual assessment. No automatic knot, lashing, frapping, strength rating or trial pass. Finished cord has no new active upkeep process; apply existing storage, condition, trial and binding wear rules, with no duplicate wear. No passive fabrication occurs while paused, studying or awaiting development. Implement guards, conservation, progress, interruption and release rules in code with regression tests for old lengths, multi-section lengths, physical refusal and resume/cancel/death idempotency; do not require repeated model adjudication.

Untying needs condition 0.5; a hugging arc loaded above half its breaking force jams. Released unretained crossings open. Joined cords wear 0.0005 per round, once. A pass means only that force for that time. No reward or rating.

candidates.function: Draw the turns of your own hand-lash-crossing lashing together with 1-3 transverse turns of its own cord between the pieces; assess, attempt, inspect, hand-test, untie or cancel; measured geometry and tensions decide results.
candidates.costs: Study: 3 rounds at 0.2. assess (frapCount 1-3 with bindingId, or with pieceIds, cordId, crossingAngle, wrapCount): 0.5, ties nothing. attempt (bindingId of your dressed lashing, frapCount): reserves it, then frapCount + 3 paid rounds of 0.5 (measure-plan, release-closure, route-frap-1..n, close-dress-release-check); resume: attempt + workId. inspect (bindingId or workId): 0.2. trial (frapped; trialForce N >0-10; trialDuration s >0-60; trialDirection): 0.5. untie: frapCount + wrapCount + 1 rounds of 0.5. cancel: free. Same room, footing and bystander rules as hand-lash-crossing. A closed lashing pauses uncharged; turns open in the hands fall loose when not worked. Refusals spend nothing; no refunds.
candidates.effects: transverse-contact@1 reuses multi-turn-contact@1 turns, closure, tensions and trials. Turns use the lashing cord: one end goes to the contact plane, round both leg bundles and back over the closure; separate or joined cord is not supported. Route: shortest found around the legs and the wedge where the gap is under the cord width, never tighter than the bend limit; later turns lie on earlier ones. Need = the longest stage incl. 0.04 m on the turn being passed, closure and 0.02 m + w tails; a measured shortfall stops before the closure opens. Each turn is snugged 5 N at its exit and falls by exp(-0.3 x contact); the push draws the legs in until their tension x d(length)/d(draw) balances it, raising each turn by stiffness x lengthening / length; the closure must hold the higher end tension. Trials use these tensions. Bound cords wear 0.0005/round once. No reward, rating, hanging load or shelter.

candidates.function: Tie an overhand knot in your own finished fiber cord with bare hands in three paid rounds, inspect it, load-trial it by its two tails, untie it, or cancel; the actual cord and its material decide results.
candidates.costs: Study: 3 rounds at 0.2 energy. targetId: exact id of your own unreserved cord or cord fragment from hand-twist-fiber-cord. attempt (knot: overhand): reserves the cord, then 3 paid rounds of 0.5 energy (lay-bend-loop, pass-end-through, dress-release-check), continuing each round; a loose undressed knot needs only the last; resume with attempt and workId only. inspect (targetId or workId): 1 round, 0.2. trial (a tied knot; trialForce N above 0 to 10; trialDuration s above 0 to 60): 1 round, 0.5. untie (a knot): 2 paid rounds of 0.5 (draw-end-back, open-loop). cancel: none. Work needs dry footing and nobody within your radius plus half the cord. Unworked rounds or low energy pause uncharged; refusals and irrelevant arguments spend nothing; nothing is refunded.
candidates.effects: Law cord-knot@1 on the same item: width = 2 ply diameters; the centreline (overall length) is conserved as two tails plus the knot path. Lobes bend no tighter than one width nor than the bend limit of the cord's material, which the first round measures; the knot path is 3 pi x lobe radius + width, centred. A loop needs a 0.02 m opening and each hand a 0.02 m pinch: a loop leaving too little end, or an end too short to pass and pinch, ends that paid stage. Dressing seats the lobes; a tail shorter than 0.02 m + width slips out on release, else the knot is tied. Trial: a 0.05 m grip per tail kept 0.01 m clear of the knot; force = min(trialForce, 200 N x health/100, 10000 N/m x width); knotted breaking force = fiber-cord breaking force / (1 + width / (2 x lobe radius)); it records extension, creep, strand damage above half that force, or a break at the knot into two owned fragments. A knot loaded by both tails cannot spill. Untying needs condition 0.5, and passes that touch after half the breaking force jam. A released untucked loop springs open. Knotted cord wears 0.0005 per round, once. A pass means only that force for that time. No reward, strength rating or extra material.

candidates.function: Bind two own branch pieces where they cross with your own fiber cord (one wrap closed by an overhand in its ends) in four paid rounds; inspect, hand-test, untie or cancel; measured pieces and cord decide results.
candidates.costs: Study: 4 rounds at 0.2 energy. attempt (pieceIds: two own untreated branch items, one whole unit each, first on top; a 2-unit lot may be named twice; cordId: own straight, unknotted, unjoined hand-twist-fiber-cord cord or fragment; crossingAngle 30-90 deg): reserves them, then 4 paid rounds of 0.5 (measure-position, route-wrap, form-tuck-closure, dress-release-check), continuing each round; a loose binding needs only the last; resume by attempt and workId. inspect (bindingId or workId): 0.2. trial (bound; trialForce N >0-10; trialDuration s >0-60; trialDirection): 0.5. untie: 2 paid rounds of 0.5. cancel: free. Needs dry footing, clear dry land for the 2 m pieces crossed at your place and nobody within your radius + 1 m. Unworked rounds, low energy or blocked room pause uncharged; refusals spend nothing; no refunds.
candidates.effects: crossing-contact@1 keeps all three items; the binding is a relation. Round 1 measures each piece by the existing branch law (2 m, 350 kg/m3 solid, water share 0.5, section from volume) and the cord: width w, cord-knot@1 bend limit R. The wrap runs in the obtuse bisector plane round both sections (ellipses r and r/sin b, offset w/2): two half perimeters + sides, routed 0.04 m loose. Closure: each end turns half round the other at Rc = max(R, w), pi Rc + w each (formed at 0.02 m opening); tails need 0.02 m + w, ends a 0.02 m pinch. A short cord, a crossing over 0.1 m thick for one hand or over 100 N x health/100 to lift: paid measured shortfall. Hand-held stages relax when interrupted. Release check: the cord-bend@1 tail rule (reed friction 0.3) must hold 5 N; then 5 N wrap tension. Trial: one hand per piece beyond the crossing; force = min(trialForce, 200 N x health/100, 10000 N/m x piece width); separate: tension max(5 N, F/2) against closure slip and cord break (fiber-cord force / (1 + w/2R)); slide: slips at 0.3 (reed on bark) x tension x top contact angle. Records bending, creep slack, damage over half breaking load, fragments. Carrying hangs the bottom piece. Untie needs condition 0.5. Bound cords wear 0.0005 per round. No reward or shelter.
